title: Contentious Topics in Fisheries & Aquaculture
description: A number of topics in fisheries, aquaculture, and marine ecology have become major points of contention in the literature, with growing bodies of evidence that appear to contradict or refute each other without resolution. This seminar introduces the main conflicting topics and key principles of the field. Students weigh the scientific evidence and discuss the broader implications of the unsettled science.

title: Foundations and Frontiers in Ecology
description: Provides an overview of fundamental concepts in ecology and discussion of recent works on these subjects. Topics include population growth and regulation, population structure, metapopulations, metacommunities, coexistence mechanisms, neutral theory, invasibility, predator-prey dynamics, disease, food webs, phenotypic plasticity, metabolic theory, and diversity-ecosystem function relationships.

title: Remote Sensing of Aquatic Environments Using the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Satellite
description: In this course, we review papers coming out from the new Surface Water and Ocean Topography Mission (SWOT) launched in December 2022. SWOT uses radar interferometry to observe sub-mesoscale eddies and small motion features on the ocean as well as water surface heights and extents from inland water bodies (lakes, wetlands, and rivers) on a global scale. Graduate students will learn about the new satellite technology, what the data is best used for, how to download the datafiles from publicly available databases, and how to apply it to their research. This course is meant to benefit both those actively using remote sensing in their work and those who are curious if they can use this data for their research.

title: Post PhD Preparation
description: This seminar explores career options for ecology and evolution PhDs, including identifying transferable skills and building industry-ready application materials. The seminar will include discussions with speakers who have pursued a variety of career paths after graduation, professionals from Career Counseling, and program alumni. The goal is to help students develop a roadmap for their career path after graduation, particularly for non-academic careers.
